org: BBC (GEL infographics guideline + BBC Visual and Data Journalism R cookbook / bbplot)
accessNotes: GEL 'How to design infographics' (redirects to /gel/features/…) read in full; its colour palettes are only in a downloadable Illustrator asset file (not opened) and an image, so no GEL hex codes are recorded. The R cookbook was read via web_fetch (truncated) and in full from its source index.Rmd on GitHub; bbplot theme values read from R/bbc_style.R and R/finalise_plot.R. The bbplot theme sets sizes in ggplot points at 640×450px output (72 dpi, so pt ≈ px). Note: bbc_style() uses Helvetica, whereas the GEL guideline specifies BBC Reith for published infographics.
summary: BBC News graphics are clean editorial charts: a large bold left-aligned headline that states the finding, a regular-weight subtitle naming the measure and period, legend at top-left without a title, light grey horizontal gridlines only, no axis titles, ticks or axis lines except a heavy dark baseline at zero, and a footer rule with 'Source: …' bottom-left and the BBC block logo bottom-right. Colour is used sparingly (signature teal-blue #1380A1 and amber #FAAB18) with direct labels and grey #555555 annotations preferred over legends.

colors.categoricalNotes: bbc_style() sets no palette; cookbook examples use #1380A1 (BBC teal-blue) for single series and the pair #FAAB18 (amber) + #1380A1 for two series, and #FAAB18, #1380A1, #990000 (dark red), #588300 (green) for four small-multiple areas. bbc_style docstring also uses #007f7f teal for a single line. Stacked proportional bars use viridis (scale_fill_viridis_d(direction = -1)). GEL: each BBC product (News, Sport, GEL) has its own infographic palette chosen to complement its brand; use a neutral palette so important information stands out; set colours for recurring things (buildings, nature) and set highlight colours.
colors.notes: Baseline/zero line and optional axis ticks #333333; gridlines #cbcbcb; annotation text and leader lines #555555; dumbbell connector #dddddd. Plot and saved background white. Viridis for ordered stacks. GEL: never convey meaning by colour alone (e.g. green/red circles combined with tick/cross icons); text must contrast with what is behind it; GEL label chips use grey, BBC red, teal and yellow fills.

typography.family: Helvetica (bbplot); BBC Reith for published GEL infographics
typography.fallback: BBC Reith Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

axisTitle.placement: omitted (axis.title = element_blank()); units go in the subtitle or in the top tick label, e.g. '80 years'

typography.notes: bbplot sizes in pt at 640×450px/72dpi: title 28 bold #222222, subtitle 22 (9pt margins above/below), legend text 18, axis text 18 (x text bottom margin 10), facet strip text 22 left-aligned, footer source 16. Annotations via geom_label size 6 (mm ≈ 17pt) in #555555, no box. Title, subtitle and caption are left-aligned to the far left of the whole graphic, not the plot panel. GEL type ramp (BBC Reith, GEL sizes): Title = Great Primer, Subheader = Great Primer, Label = Pica, Source = Brevier.

structure.gridlines: Major horizontal (y) gridlines only, solid #cbcbcb; no minor gridlines; for horizontal bar charts switch to vertical (x) gridlines in #cbcbcb.
structure.ticks: No ticks by default; cookbook shows adding x ticks in #333333 when needed (e.g. dates).
structure.zeroLine: Yes — signature heavy baseline: geom_hline(yintercept = 0, size = 1, colour = '#333333') on every chart (vertical baseline for horizontal bars).
structure.yAxisTitle: omitted; unit in subtitle or appended to the top tick label ('80 years', '6%')
structure.unitPlacement: in subtitle (e.g. 'Yuan per tonne' as a separate line above the axis in GEL example) or on the last tick label
structure.frame: none; full-width footer rule above source/logo
structure.background: white (panel background blank, saved with bg = 'white')
structure.notes: Facet strips white with 22pt left-aligned titles.

legend.placement: top, left-aligned (legend.position 'top'; cookbook nudges it flush left with legend.justification 'left' or negative margin)
legend.directLabels: Preferred: 'Remove the legend to become one — it's better to label data directly with text annotations' — labels in the series colour next to line ends.
legend.title: none (legend.title blank)
legend.notes: Legend text 18pt #222222; extra spacing between items via padded labels; reverse order to match stacks.

marks.bars: Flat fill #1380A1, no outline; horizontal bars (coord_flip) for ranked categories with value labels inside bar ends in white; histograms with white bar outlines; stacked/grouped bars via position fill/dodge.
marks.lines: 1pt-ish (ggplot size = 1) lines in #1380A1 / #FAAB18; no point markers.
marks.areas: Solid fills in palette colours for small multiples.
marks.points: Scatter/bubble points with thin dark outlines in BBC examples; dumbbells: #dddddd connector size 3 with #FAAB18 and #1380A1 end dots.
marks.pies: GEL lists pie charts among common forms; no specific rules.

labels.dataLabels: Bar values printed inside the bar end (hjust = 1) or at the bar start (left-aligned), white text, no label box, size 6 Helvetica.
labels.numberFormat: Thousand separators with commas (scales::comma); percentages via paste0(x, '%'); custom tick labels with unit on the last tick ('80 years'); billions abbreviated '2bn'.
labels.dates: Year ticks, with abbreviated two-digit years after the first ('2009, 10, 11 … 2016') in GEL example; 'Mar 2009 – Oct 2015' style ranges in subtitles.

furniture.title: Headline states the takeaway in few words ('Living longer', 'Reunion is highest', 'Asia's rapid growth'); subtitle states measure, place and period ('Life expectancy in China 1952-2007').
furniture.source: finalise_plot draws a thin full-width rule, then the source text bottom-left at 16pt; text must be typed as 'Source: …' (e.g. 'Source: Gapminder').
furniture.logo: BBC block logo (three boxed letters) bottom-right in the footer, same line as the source.
furniture.other: Default export 640×450px (taller e.g. 640×550 when needed); title/subtitle/caption left-aligned to the graphic edge.

annotations: Plain text annotations (geom_label without box, label.size = NA) in #555555 at size 6, left-justified, multi-line allowed; leader lines/curved lines and arrows in #555555 size 0.5 (curvature −0.2, small arrowheads); dashed vertical/horizontal reference lines for thresholds. GEL label styles: grey or coloured (red, teal, yellow) chip labels — beaked labels and pointer labels with a stem ending in a filled or open circle, and area labels.
layout: bbplot exports at 640×450px. GEL responsive infographics are drawn at fixed widths with variable depth: small 400px (0–400 devices), medium 750px (401–750), large 976px (751–976+); small is a vertical stack, medium/large horizontal layouts. Less detail as images get smaller.
accessibility: Text alternatives for every image infographic; don't rely on colour alone (pair colour with shapes, patterns or icons); text colour must meet contrast guidelines; follow BBC mobile accessibility guidelines.

chartTypes.notes: GEL: four infographic categories — diagrams, data visualisation, annotations, maps.

distinctiveRules.rule: Every chart gets a heavy dark baseline at zero: 1-size solid line #333333 (vertical for horizontal bars).
distinctiveRules.quote: our design style … is to add a vertical or horizontal baseline to our charts: geom_hline(yintercept = 0, size = 1, colour = "#333333")

distinctiveRules.rule: Only major horizontal gridlines in light grey #cbcbcb; no minor gridlines, no axis lines, no ticks.
distinctiveRules.quote: panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color="#cbcbcb"), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), axis.line = element_blank()

distinctiveRules.rule: No axis titles; units go in the subtitle or are appended to the top tick label (e.g. '80 years').
Title 28pt bold #222222, subtitle 22pt regular, both flush-left to the edge of the whole graphic (not the plot panel).
distinctiveRules.quote: plot.title size=28 face="bold" color="#222222"; left_align(plot_name, c("subtitle", "title", "caption"))

distinctiveRules.rule: Headline states the finding in a few words; subtitle gives measure, place and period.
distinctiveRules.quote: labs(title="Living longer", subtitle = "Life expectancy in China 1952-2007")

distinctiveRules.rule: Footer: thin full-width rule, then 'Source: …' at 16pt bottom-left and the BBC block logo bottom-right on the same line.
distinctiveRules.quote: linesGrob(x = c(0, 1)) … textGrob(source_name, x = 0.004, hjust = 0, fontsize=16) … rasterGrob(logo, x = 0.944)

distinctiveRules.rule: Legend at top, left-aligned, with no legend title and 18pt labels — or better, removed in favour of direct labels.
distinctiveRules.quote: legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank() … it's better to label data directly with text annotations

distinctiveRules.rule: Single-series marks in BBC teal-blue #1380A1; two series as #FAAB18 amber vs #1380A1.
Annotations are box-less grey #555555 text with thin #555555 curved leader lines/arrows.
distinctiveRules.quote: geom_label(…, colour = "#555555", label.size = NA, size = 6) … geom_curve(…, colour = "#555555", size=0.5, curvature = -0.2, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.03, "npc")))

distinctiveRules.rule: Bar value labels in white inside the bar end (or at the bar start), no label box.
distinctiveRules.quote: geom_label(aes(label = round(lifeExp, 0)), hjust = 1, colour = "white", fill = NA, label.size = NA)

distinctiveRules.rule: Ranked horizontal bars switch gridlines to vertical (#cbcbcb) and remove horizontal ones.
Default export size 640×450px; responsive infographics at fixed widths 400 / 750 / 976px with variable height.
distinctiveRules.quote: Graphic width (px) 400 750 976 … we do not have fixed depths

distinctiveRules.rule: Published infographics use BBC Reith with the GEL type ramp: title and subheader Great Primer, labels Pica, source Brevier.
distinctiveRules.quote: BBC Reith is used as our main typeface for all infographics … Title Great primer, Subheader Great primer, Label Pica, Source Brevier

distinctiveRules.rule: Neutral palette with colour reserved for the key information; meaning never by colour alone (pair with icons/shapes).
distinctiveRules.quote: Use a neutral colour palette so important information stands out more in comparison. Don't convey meaning with colour alone.

referenceImages.describes: Composite of five published BBC News charts made with bbplot. Each has a large bold black left-aligned headline ('Blue wave', 'Where penalties are saved', 'MPs rejected Theresa May's deal by 230 votes', 'Fast-growing cities face worse climate risks', 'Earnings vary across unis even within subjects') with a regular subtitle beneath; legends top-left with square or circle keys and no title; light grey horizontal gridlines only; heavy black baseline at 0 (histograms) or vertical zero line (dumbbells); no axis titles except plain-language end labels ('Less vulnerable'/'More vulnerable', 'Below average ←/→ Above average'); grey annotation text with thin curved leader lines and arrows; direct labels in series colours (orange/teal on dumbbells). Footer: thin rule, 'Source: AP, 19:01 ET' bottom-left in regular grey-black, and the boxed 'BBC' block logo bottom-right. Colours: BBC blue/light blue, red/pink, orange dots, party colours, region colours (red, amber, teal, purple, green).

GEL example line graph from BBC News in BBC Reith: regular-weight title 'Price of steel Mar 2009 – Oct 2015' top-left, then a separate unit line 'Yuan per tonne' above the y axis (horizontal, not rotated). Single thick teal line, no markers. Light grey horizontal gridlines at 1,000 steps with comma separators; y labels left; solid dark x-axis baseline with downward ticks; year labels '2009, 10, 11 … 15, 2016' (full year only at ends). No legend, source not shown in crop.

GEL infographic label styles in BBC Reith: 'beaked' chip labels (light grey with dark text, or BBC red with white text) with a downward triangular beak; 'pointer' labels — rectangular chips (grey, teal with white text, yellow with dark text) with a dark underline rule and a vertical stem ending in a filled or open circle; 'area' labels — grey chip attached by a stem to an outlined circle, square or rectangle.
